topic: Azure Capacity Reservation economics for GPU VM SKUs such as NVads A10 v5

claims.claim: Azure Capacity Reservation is billed at the same rate as the underlying VM size whether the reserved capacity is used or unused.

support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: Capacity reservations are priced at the same rate as the underlying VM size, and billing starts even if the reservation is not being used.
Azure charges for the selected VM size at pay-as-you-go rates whether the VM was provisioned or not.

claims.claim: Capacity reservations can be created and deleted without a fixed term commitment.

support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: You do not have to sign up for a one-year or three-year term commitment, and you can create and delete reservations at any time.

claims.claim: A capacity reservation is defined by VM size, location, and quantity.

support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: The overview lists VM size, location or zone, and quantity of instances reserved as the basic properties defined at creation time.

claims.claim: Reserved Instances and Savings Plan discounts can apply to both used and unused capacity reservation usage.

support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: Both used and unused capacity reservations are eligible for Savings Plan and Reserved Instances term commitment discounts.
Reserved VM instances can cover some or all capacity reservation usage even when VMs are not deployed.

claims.claim: Capacity is guaranteed only while the reservation exists. Once the reservation is deleted, Azure no longer documents that capacity as reserved for you, and a future reservation request may fail if capacity is unavailable.

support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: The overview says capacity is reserved for your use until the reservation is deleted.
After the reservation is deleted, you do not pay for it anymore, and any later reservation creation requires a new successful capacity request.

claims.claim: Capacity Reservation is different from Reserved Instances. Capacity Reservation secures capacity availability, while Reserved Instances provide a billing discount and do not guarantee capacity.

support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: The comparison table says Capacity Reservation provides a capacity guarantee, while Reserved Instances provide significant cost savings but do not provide a capacity guarantee.

support.source_title: Save costs with Azure Reserved VM Instances
support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: Reserved VM instances provide a billing discount only and do not reserve or guarantee compute capacity.

claims.claim: The NVads A10 v5 series is listed in Microsoft Learn among the GPU-accelerated compute series that support Capacity Reservation.

support.support_quote_or_paraphrase: The GPU-accelerated compute list includes NVadsA10_v5 series among the VM series that support creation of capacity reservations.

open_questions.item: Exact public list prices used for the illustrative EUR 123k to EUR 204k range
open_questions.note: The article marks this range as assumption-based and not an official quote.
The article avoids region-specific scarcity claims and frames reacquisition risk as the practical implication of documented capacity checks.
